title: Lint, publish, install: PSScriptAnalyzer and PSResourceGet
summary: Make PSScriptAnalyzer a CI gate with a settings file, fix the findings that matter (plain-text passwords), and publish and install your module through a feed with PSResourceGet.

steps.title: PSScriptAnalyzer as a gate
body: **PSScriptAnalyzer** (1.25 is current) is the linter behind the VS Code PowerShell extension's squiggles. In CI you
run it with a **settings file** checked into the repo, so everyone (and the pipeline) applies the same rules:
```powershell
# PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1
Severity     = @('Error', 'Warning')
ExcludeRules = @('PSAvoidUsingWriteHost')     # this repo's scripts are interactive tools
```powershell
Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer -Path . -Recurse -Settings ./PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1 -EnableExit
`-EnableExit` sets the exit code to the number of findings, so the build fails on any. Findings worth knowing by name:
| Rule | Why it matters |
| `PSAvoidUsingPlainTextForPassword` | a `[string] $Password` parameter ends up in history, logs and process lists |
| `PSAvoidUsingConvertToSecureStringWithPlainText` | the secret is in the script or its caller in clear text |
| `PSUseDeclaredVarsMoreThanAssignments` | a variable set and never used: usually a typo or dead code |
| `PSUseShouldProcessForStateChangingFunctions` | `Remove-`/`Set-`/`New-` functions without `-WhatIf` |
| `PSAvoidUsingCmdletAliases` | aliases differ between machines |
The right type for a secret parameter is **`[pscredential]`** (user name plus `SecureString`), filled by
`Get-Credential` interactively or by a secret store in automation (module 7).

steps.title: Make the analyzer gate pass, honestly
prompt: 1. Create `~/scripts/PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1` that reports **Error and Warning** findings and excludes only
2. Fix the script, do not silence it: take a **`[pscredential] $Credential`** parameter instead of `-UserName` and
must then exit `0`, and the script must still print `would mount \\files.example.com\reports as <user>`.

checks.name: the settings file has the right rules
checks.fail: The settings file should set `Severity = @('Error', 'Warning')` and `ExcludeRules = @('PSAvoidUsingWriteHost')`, nothing else excluded.

checks.name: the gate passes
checks.fail: PSScriptAnalyzer still reports findings (below). Fix the code rather than excluding more rules.

checks.name: it takes a PSCredential and still works

hints: The settings file is a plain hashtable: `@{ Severity = @('Error', 'Warning'); ExcludeRules = @('PSAvoidUsingWriteHost') }`.
The new `param()`: `[Parameter(Mandatory)] [pscredential] $Credential`. Then `ConvertTo-SecureString`, `$secure`, `$credential = ...` and `$unused` all go.
Keep the last line, but use `$Credential.UserName`.
solution: # Mount-ReportShare.ps1: connects the reports share for the month-end job.
explain: The test in the check builds a credential from a plain string, which is fine in a test and nowhere else. In the
real job the credential comes from `Get-Secret` (module 7). A `[pscredential]` parameter also works with
`New-PSDrive -Credential`, `Invoke-Command -Credential` and most cmdlets that log in somewhere.

steps.title: PSResourceGet: the current way to install modules
body: **PSResourceGet** (`Microsoft.PowerShell.PSResourceGet`, bundled since PowerShell 7.4; 1.2.1 ships with 7.6) replaces
the old **PowerShellGet 2** (`Install-Module`, `Find-Module`), which is still in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and in many
scripts. Same ideas, new names:
| Job | PowerShellGet 2 (old) | PSResourceGet (current) |
| Search | `Find-Module` | `Find-PSResource` |
| Install | `Install-Module -Scope CurrentUser` | `Install-PSResource -Scope CurrentUser` |
| Download only | `Save-Module` | `Save-PSResource` |
| What is installed | `Get-InstalledModule` | `Get-InstalledPSResource` |
| Publish | `Publish-Module` | `Publish-PSResource` |
| Add a feed | `Register-PSRepository` | `Register-PSResourceRepository` |
**Trust.** The PowerShell Gallery is public: anyone can publish, and name-squatting and malicious packages happen.
`PSGallery` is **untrusted** by default, so installs ask first. Teams usually: pin versions (`-Version '[2.1.0, 3.0)'`
or an exact one), vet a module once and mirror it to an **internal feed** (a NuGet server, Azure Artifacts, or even
a file share), and install from there with `-TrustRepository` only for that feed. `Save-PSResource` is also how you
get modules onto a server with no internet.

steps.explain: Both are still everywhere. In new scripts, use PSResourceGet; on a Windows PowerShell 5.1 box without it, `Install-Module` is what you have (and `Install-PSResource -Name Microsoft.PowerShell.PSResourceGet` fixes that).

steps.title: Publish LogTools to the team feed and install it
prompt: The team keeps vetted modules in a feed. Here it is a folder, `~/feed` (a file share works the same way).
1. Register it as a repository named **`TeamFeed`**, **trusted** (leave `PSGallery` untrusted).
2. Bump LogTools to **1.1.0** in its manifest, and **publish** `~/src/LogTools` to `TeamFeed`.

checks.name: TeamFeed is registered and trusted, PSGallery is not
checks.cmd: pwsh -NoProfile -c '$f = Get-PSResourceRepository TeamFeed -ErrorAction Stop; $g = Get-PSResourceRepository PSGallery; "$($f.Uri.LocalPath.TrimEnd("/")) $($f.Trusted) $($g.Trusted)"'
checks.fail: `Get-PSResourceRepository` should show `TeamFeed` at `/home/learner/feed`, trusted, and `PSGallery` still untrusted.

hints: `Install-PSResource -Name LogTools -Repository TeamFeed -Scope CurrentUser`, and check with `Get-InstalledPSResource LogTools`.
explain: In a real pipeline, the publish step runs only after Pester and PSScriptAnalyzer pass, with the feed's API key from
the pipeline's secret store (`Publish-PSResource -ApiKey`), and every machine installs from the feed with a pinned
version. A `RequiredModules` entry in a manifest, or `#Requires -Modules`, then fails fast on a machine that does

steps.prompt: A blog post says: `Install-Module CoolTools -Force -SkipPublisherCheck -AllowClobber`. Before running it on a build server, what is the most important thing to check?
options: Who publishes CoolTools and what it does (Gallery page, source, downloads), and pin a version or mirror it to your feed
Nothing: the Gallery scans every package
steps.explain: `-Force -SkipPublisherCheck -AllowClobber` turns off the very prompts that protect you: replacing commands from other modules and ignoring a changed signing publisher. Module code runs with the server's permissions. Gallery packages are checked for known malware, not for being safe or trustworthy.
